subject: Re: FinchBank: request for auditable model change logs
body:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 9:44 AM PST
Subject: FinchBank: request for auditable model change logs

Hey Connor,

FinchBank is in security/procurement and just sent over a third-party risk questionnaire section specifically about “model update/change logging.” Their key ask is: auditable + immutable model release notes (who/what/when), with a retention commitment, and a way for them to consume updates (API/feed preferred).

I know this overlaps directly with the schema + model changelog work your team is driving. Can you help me with:

1) What we can credibly commit to near-term (next 4–8 weeks) vs what’s later.
2) Any customer-safe description of the approach (source of truth, approvals, audit trail).
3) Whether we can offer them early access/beta to the feed/Console changelog.

They’re pushing for something stronger than “we post docs updates sometimes,” which is fair.

I attached their questionnaire + the PDF excerpt they highlighted.

Thanks,
Ava

—
Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference



From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 10:12 AM PST
Subject: Re: FinchBank: request for auditable model change logs

Hey Ava — yep, this is exactly the pain point we’re trying to solve.

High level (customer-safe):
- We’re moving to a single source of truth for model version metadata in the model registry.
- Every create/update/deprecation emits a signed change event (actor + timestamp + event_id + diff).
- Customer-visible release notes are generated from those events with a review/approval workflow prior to publish.
- Published entries are immutable; corrections are handled via a superseding entry so history is preserved.

Near-term vs later:
- Near-term (targeting a beta): published model changelog in docs + Console tab, plus a machine-readable feed endpoint.
- Later hardening: longer retention guarantees, SIEM export packaging, and a few edge cases around backfilled historical notes.

Two quick questions so I can tailor what to send back:
1) Are they asking for audit logs about *customer-visible* notes only, or also internal metadata edits?
2) Do they require on-demand export (e.g., PDF) or is a JSON feed acceptable for their change mgmt?

If you can forward the exact questions they’re asking (or paste the section), I’ll draft answers aligned with what we can actually deliver.

Connor

—
Connor O'Brien
Release Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 10:46 AM PST
Subject: Re: FinchBank: request for auditable model change logs

Thanks — super helpful.

Here are the exact questions they pulled out (copy/pasted from their doc). They care about both the external “release notes” and the internal accountability trail.

Questions:
1) “Does the vendor maintain an immutable audit log of model changes (including version changes, weight updates, quantization changes, or serving configuration changes)?”
2) “For each model change, can the vendor provide: unique change ID, timestamp, approver, and a customer-consumable summary of impact?”
3) “What is the minimum retention period for model change logs and associated audit events?”
4) “Can the customer subscribe to change events (API, RSS/Atom, webhook)?”
5) “Can changes be rolled back? If so, how is the rollback communicated and audited?”

They explicitly mention their internal change advisory board (CAB) wants an evidence trail for audits.

They said JSON feed is acceptable as long as it’s stable + has ETags/caching; PDF export is a “nice to have.”

Also: they asked if we can commit to a deprecation notice window (they said 90 days is their default expectation).

Ava



From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 12:03 PM PST
Subject: Re: FinchBank: request for auditable model change logs

Perfect. Below is draft language you can reuse (feel free to edit for tone). I’m keeping it customer-safe + aligned to what we’re implementing.

---
Draft responses (FinchBank):

1) Immutable audit log of model changes
We are implementing an auditable change log for model versions served through Redwood. Changes to model version metadata (including compatibility fields and deprecation state) are recorded as append-only change events with a unique event ID, timestamp, and actor identity. Customer-visible entries are published from those events via a controlled workflow.

Note: some operational serving configuration changes may be represented separately from customer-facing release notes; our goal is that any change that could affect customer experience (compatibility, routing, availability, deprecations, pinned version behavior) is captured with a corresponding changelog entry.

2) Unique change ID, timestamp, approver, and customer summary
Yes. Each published changelog entry references the underlying event_id and includes: publish timestamp, review/approval state, and a customer-facing summary that includes impact/compatibility notes and any required actions.

3) Retention period
We maintain retention for changelog entries and associated audit events per our security/compliance controls. For enterprise accounts, we can discuss a retention commitment appropriate to your audit requirements (e.g., multi-year retention).

(Internal note for us: I need to confirm the exact retention number we can promise in writing — do you have a minimum they’re expecting beyond “multi-year”?)

4) Subscription to change events
We will provide a machine-readable feed endpoint for published changelog entries and will also provide docs-based access. RSS/Atom is on the roadmap; webhook delivery is not part of the initial beta.

5) Rollback and audit
If a published entry is incorrect, we do not overwrite history. We publish a superseding corrected entry and preserve the original entry for auditability. Operational rollbacks (e.g., reverting a model version used in a deployment) are communicated via the published changelog entry associated with that change.

Deprecation notice window
We intend to provide clear deprecation timelines in the changelog. Standard windows may vary by model and change type; we can align on notice windows for regulated workflows as part of the enterprise change-management process.
---

Two things I’d like you to avoid committing to unless we get a quick internal OK:
- A specific retention duration (e.g., “7 years”) without Compliance signing off.
- “Webhooks available today.” We can say feed endpoint + RSS planned.

If you want, I can jump on a 20 min call with them to walk through our approach.

Connor
